paper.title_en: The generalized Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution and its application on the Jeans mass
paper.abstract_en: The classical Jeans mass criterion describes the gravitational collapse of a homogeneous self-gravitating gas cloud using the Maxwell-Boltzmann velocity distribution. However, the standard formulation does not adequately explain the observed instability of several Bok globules whose measured masses lie below the classical Jeans threshold. We derive a generalized Jeans mass, $M_J(\gamma)$, from first principles by replacing the ordinary Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution with a Mittag-Leffler modified Maxwell-Boltzmann (MLMB) distribution. The deformation parameter $\gamma$ characterizes departures from classical statistical mechanics. For appropriate critical values of $\gamma$, the resulting generalized Jeans mass reproduces the observed masses of unstable Bok globules and resolves the discrepancy with the classical criterion. The predictions are also in quantitative agreement with alternative approaches based on dark-matter backgrounds and modified-gravity models. The MLMB framework therefore provides a statistical-mechanical description of gravitational instability in which $\gamma$ effectively parametrizes the complex internal dynamics of molecular clouds.
